title: Who Carries the Sacred Tent
overview: This chapter assigns the Levite clans their exact jobs for taking down, carrying and guarding Israel's portable worship tent whenever the camp moved.

parts.label: Counting the Kohathites (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: The Levites, the tribe set apart for worship duties, are counted again, this time only the men aged 30 to 50 who were fit for the hard work. The Kohathite clan gets the most sensitive job: carrying the most sacred objects of the tent of meeting, Israel's portable worship tent.

parts.label: Wrapping the holy objects (vv. 5-14)
parts.note: Before each move, only the priests, Aaron and his sons, go in and wrap the ark (the sacred chest of the covenant), the bread table, the lampstand and the two altars. Layers of colored cloth and a tough outer leather protect each piece from weather and hide it from view, though which animal the leather came from is uncertain.

parts.label: Carry but do not touch (vv. 15-16)
parts.note: The Kohathites carry the wrapped objects on poles or carrying frames, but touching the holy things themselves would mean death. Aaron's son Eleazar oversees everything and personally keeps the lamp oil, incense, daily grain offering and anointing oil.

parts.label: Keeping the Kohathites alive (vv. 17-20)
parts.note: The priests must protect the Kohathites by giving each man his exact load, so no one goes in or even glances at the uncovered objects. The text treats holiness as truly dangerous, and later books tell of people who died for handling the ark wrongly.

parts.label: Gershonites and Merarites (vv. 21-33)
parts.note: The Gershonites carry the fabric: curtains, coverings, entrance screens and ropes. The Merarites carry the heavy frames, posts, bases and tent pegs, each item assigned to a named man, and both clans work under Aaron's son Ithamar.

parts.label: The final count (vv. 34-49)
parts.note: The working Levites total 8,580, and the Merarites, who had the heaviest loads, are the largest group. Every man is counted and given his task, just as the chapter says the LORD commanded.

think: What do you think is gained or lost when something is treated as too sacred to touch or even look at?
